checks.invariant: Voice capture must have an effective frame/deadline bound and a stop path; do not equate an optional local recording defect with a demonstrated shared-service denial.
checks.result: vad.py17/42-45 declares a12s default/frame budget, but positive speech appends and continues69-74 before the only length check85; after speech begins, empty-queue exceptions61-63 ignore the deadline. The callback queue31/36 is unbounded. wake_word.py116/203/209 calls the recorder without timeout or stop token; outer listen deadline80 does not execute during nested capture. The wake callback queue60/66 can also accumulate while nested VAD holds its input-stream context. VoicePipeline.stop47-50 only sets an event, which run58 checks outside the blocking to_thread(wake_word.listen)64. Missing audio dependencies fail closed at vad.py21-26, and wake/listen exceptions return empty audio119-121. Push-to-talk release clears its own event but does not signal the active recorder. These are concrete resource/cancellation weaknesses; no actual hostile microphone input, deployed voice enablement or shared-service availability loss was demonstrated.

hardening: Fix the demonstrated recorder cap defect at app/voice/vad.py57-86: check an unconditional monotonic deadline and recorded-frame/byte budget on every iteration, including speech, malformed frames and queue timeouts. The finite fixture returned42 frames for a20-frame cap. Add regression cases for continuous speech and post-speech input loss; do not describe this fixture as a reproduced shared-service DoS.

Pass a cancellation event through VoicePipeline.run -> WakeWordDetector.listen -> VoiceActivityDetector.record_until_silence and check it in capture/queue loops; close capture resources promptly when VoicePipeline.stop is requested. Present stop signaling cannot interrupt an already active recorder.

Bound callback queues in both app/voice/vad.py31 and wake_word.py60, with an explicit drop/backpressure policy that cannot block the real-time audio callback. Exit the wake input-stream context before starting a separate VAD stream, so the unused wake queue does not keep buffering the whole utterance.

Security severity is intentionally unassigned: local optional microphone control-flow and buffering defects are source/local-established, but no lower-trust principal caused a demonstrated shared-service availability or safety loss in this audit. A deployment-level claim would require an enabled voice runtime and a bounded, approved observation of the specific affected safety/availability function.
